messages.author: d85549b942e39c52
messages.subject: buildMCMC taking days to run
parts:
Hello nimble-users,

I am relatively new to nimble but have some prior experience running single season SCR models in nimble. I am now working on a CJS model with 7 years of spatial capture recapture data at 201 sites, up to 8 sampling occasions (weeks), and 300 individuals (detected + augmented). My model has been stuck on the buildMCMC() stage for >3 days and I'm wondering if this normal behavior for larger models like this or an indication that something is wrong? Everything in the model looked good prior to this stage. I cannot share the data in this forum, but may be able to in a private message thread if needed. 

Thanks in advance!
Erika

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: buildMCMC taking days to run
parts:
Hi Erika,

Thanks for the question. Obviously running for >3 days in a setup step does not sound good. We've made a lot of improvements over the years in efficiency of these steps but there can still be cases that get bogged down, although that would be rather extreme. The most common suspect would be a model with long chains of deterministic nodes between stochastic nodes. Can you please try using the argument "useConjugacy=FALSE" in configureMCMC (or, if you are skipping configureMCMC and going straight to straight to buildMCMC, provide the argument there). If that doesn't help, the only way someone could really figure out what is happening is if you can send a reproducible example, with data, off-list if you prefer. It is also conceivable that something is wrong with your model that is not being caught and that is somehow spinning the system so badly, although I'm not sure exactly how that would happen. 

Perry

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: buildMCMC taking days to run
parts:
Hi Erika,

Thanks for sending your full example off-list. Too bad turning off conjugacy checking did not help.

I've taken a look and (as you described) your case is a good-sized spatial capture-recapture model. In SCR models, objects can get large quickly due to distances between every individual and every detector location. Your case also has time and (I think) life stage. This is giving roughly (I think) 10.5 million nodes, some in single variables with 3.4 million nodes. Basically, nimble does not scale well for this problem. Some of the deep rewriting we're doing should help in the future, but that won't help you now.

Have you checked out nimbleSCR and Efficient Estimation of Large-Scale Spatial Capture-Recapture Models? These give nimbleFunctions, more compact data structures, and other tricks that can help a great deal. I also noticed that you could consider removing some of the posterior predictive components and obtaining those later. Also (if I am not being too hasty) the NAs in your data matrix will result in samplers to update those values as missing data. I think there were quite a large proportion of those. If you don't really need those imputed as missing data, you could greatly reduce the number of samplers needed by not including those. Finally I noticed a covariate with many NAs. If you have a way to set up "previous" in a smaller way (because it is quite sparse), that could help.

Sorry I don't have a quicker fix for you.

HTH
Perry

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: buildMCMC taking days to run
parts:
Hi Victor,
nimble does have scaling problems for large models. One of the main issues for scaling is the number of nodes in the directed acyclic graph defined by the model. Sometimes it is possible to vectorize (reducing the number of nodes because many scalar nodes can become one vector node) and/or to put some calculations inside nimbleFunctions to reduce a need for some nodes in the model itself. I think we'd have to see your code to make more specific suggestions.
Perry
